title: The 2026 Alpöge claim of a proof of RH and GRH, and Nielsen's objection
claimant: Levent Alpöge, with Claude; the formalisation released as a Lean 4 library
statement: "also formalized the arguments without assumptions": a statement of belief that the author, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, that the method extends to the generalised Riemann hypothesis, and that the argument has been formalised in Lean 4 with no assumptions beyond Mathlib's.
statement_location: references/alpoge_remark_2026-11-20.pdf, p. 1. The document is four pages and contains no mathematics: it states the belief, gives a timeline of the argument, and says why the medium was Lean rather than a paper ("It being obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of 'slop', I decided to only present Lean.").

formal.role: this repository's recording of the dispute (live)
formal.note: This is not a model of the published proof and it is not offered as one. It is the repository's own file: it states Alpoge's position with `sorry` and proves the structural core of Nielsen's objection without one. Running the five questions on it is a live negative control, and the `sorry` the agent finds is the one the record says is there. Its two trace requests are a positive and a negative control for the dependency trace itself: `geometry_is_vacuous` must reach `vacuousGeometry`, and `closed_false_impossible` must not.

mutants.note: the theorem asserts the vacuous predicate of every input, so flipping it to `False` must break that theorem: a kill here is the engine's positive control
same rewrite, different theorem: this one never mentions the vacuous predicate, so it must survive. The pair is the negative control, and it is what 'not load-bearing' looks like mechanically
the structure of Nielsen's objection as a theorem: the hypothesis `h` is used by `rw`, so weakening it to `True` must kill the proof. A survivor here would mean the hypothesis does no work

institutional.value: no journal article exists as of 2026-11-22; the primary document is a four-page personal remark that states no mathematics
institutional.note: There is no prose argument to review, which is why the level-1 instruments have no declared inputs to classify.

institutional.value: the Lean and Mathlib communities jointly stated "We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct", and that all four Xena Project criteria are satisfied
institutional.note: A statement about a statement and a term, by parties who maintain the library the term is stated in.

institutional.value: Drew Sutherland's verification page records the mechanical audit: 175,187 modules compile; `#print axioms` for the five headline theorems returns only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; the 15 axioms in the environment are all in `Init`; Mathlib's compiled artefacts are byte-identical to the official cache; a sandboxed rebuild reproduces the 61,570,595,788-byte export byte for byte; `leanchecker` replays 175,187 of 175,187 modules with zero rejections; nanoda and con-leche (and con-ron, its Rust port) accept the export, con-leche reporting 1,468,418 declarations accepted in `--verified` mode and all five challenge theorems justified by the solution. Its own caveat is that a passing check relies on those kernels and on Mathlib's definitions being what they are intended to be, and its scope note is that GRH there means Dirichlet L-functions: Dedekind, Hecke and automorphic L-functions were not among the statements checked.
institutional.note: A checklist of kernel checks that were run, not an independent formalisation of the argument, and not a dependency analysis: it says nothing about whether the proof routes through definitions that carry no mathematics, and it states that limit itself.

institutional.value: reproduced here: `con-leche --verified` accepted 1,468,418 declarations with exit 0 in 561.6 s, and `--compare` justified all five challenge theorems; the challenge alone fails with `sorryAx` as a negative control
institutional.note: One independent checker, not three: nanoda and leanchecker were not run, and the report says so.

institutional.value: Nielsen's 13-page objection, not peer-reviewed, states that the formalisation discharges its geometry obligations vacuously
institutional.note: Her Appendix A states that she does not show the term fails to typecheck, nor that `RiemannHypothesis` is underivable.

institutional.value: the Riemann hypothesis remains one of the Clay Mathematics Institute's Millennium Prize Problems and the prize is unawarded
institutional.note: A preprint and a formalisation do not change this status; only the Institute's own process can, and it has not run.

objections.source: Nielsen, The Invalidity of Alpöge's Proposed Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis (2026-11-20), §8 and §9
objections.summary: the geometry predicate the formalisation routes through is constantly `True` (`anyGeometry := fun _ _ _ => True`), so the obligations it discharges carry no geometry and the conclusion establishes nothing
objections.decisive_question: does the compiled dependency chain of the final theorem pass through `anyGeometry`, `geoDegenerate`, `divXFl` or `x0`? A walk of the exported dependency graph answers it; reading 70 of 175,187 source files does not, and this repository does not hold the archive.

objections.source: Chu, third-party audit of the code claims (2026-11-22)
objections.summary: agrees that `anyGeometry` is `fun _ _ _ => True`, that it reaches 24 files, and that `GeoCl.base` discharges every obligation with `trivial`; disputes Nielsen's reading of the `degenerate` names as the release's own, reporting every `degenerate` hit as the ordinary word `nondegenerate`
objections.decisive_question: a case-sensitive count of `geoDegenerate` over the archive. One of the two sides is wrong about a search that takes one command, and neither has published the count with the command that produced it.

notes: The claim declares no inputs in the Davenport-Heilbronn filter's sense, and that is a fact about the release rather than about the argument: the published material is a Lean library, so there is no prose inventory of assumptions to classify. The filter therefore returns `needs_sourcing` (an undeclared candidate is unscreened, not dead) and the numerical instruments return `outside domain`. The non-vacuity question is the only one in this record that nothing in the repository can decide, and it is the one that matters.
